point-object.def: The object model: treating an object as a single point that has a position but no size, shape or inner parts. It works when those do not affect the motion described.

time-interval.def: The time between two moments: Δt = t(final) − t(initial), in seconds.

average-velocity.def: Displacement divided by the time interval: v(avg) = Δx/Δt, in m/s. Its sign gives the direction of the net change in position.

acceleration.def: The rate at which velocity changes, in m/s². An object accelerates when its speed changes, its direction changes, or both.

average-acceleration.def: Change in velocity divided by the time interval: a(avg) = Δv/Δt, in m/s². It points the same way as Δv.

instantaneous-velocity.def: The velocity at one instant: the value the average velocity approaches as the time interval is made very short.

instantaneous-acceleration.def: The acceleration at one instant: the value the average acceleration approaches as the time interval is made very short.
